text:
mika: Hey folks — trying the starter 'hello world' quickstart and it hangs right after the first npm start. Browser shows streaming websocket connect then a 403, then the app logs show 'token not found in cache'. Using Node 18 on macOS, env var REDWOOD_API_KEY is set. Anyone seen this? :confused:

devex-bot: Ticket created: DEVEX-5189. Please include a short reproducer and logs.

jordan: Can you paste the terminal output around the 403? Also which quickstart repo (node/js/python)?

mika: node quickstart (github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart-node). Terminal snippet:
```
> npm run start
Server listening on http://localhost:3000
[2026-03-22T12:01:02Z] INFO: connecting to api...
[2026-03-22T12:01:02Z] ERROR: request failed 403 Forbidden
Error: token not found in cache
    at refreshAuth (/app/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/auth.js:112)
```

lee: That 'token not found in cache' looks like the SDK tried to use the cached service token but it wasn't available, then refresh attempted and the refresh got 403. Two common causes: 1) env var is actually a workspace-scoped key that needs a different header, 2) org hasn't completed billing/terms and first-call is gated.

mika: ohhh. I thought REDWOOD_API_KEY was enough for local quickstarts. How do I check the org gating?

sam: Go to https://console.redwood.ai/orgs in your account and look for the banner about billing or trial. If you signed up via invite you sometimes need to accept org terms before first-call. If it's gated you'll see 'First-call blocked: billing required'.

mika: Confirmed — console shows "Accept billing/terms to enable API calls". I didn't realize that blocks the SDK refresh flow. Is there a local bypass for dev?

jordan: We intentionally gate production keys, but for local dev we should support ephemeral dev keys. Short-term workaround: generate a personal API key in the console (Profile -> API keys) and set REDWOOD_API_KEY to that. That key isn't org-gated the same way.

lee: Another quick workaround is to use the CLI auth flow: `npx @redwood/cli login` — it opens a browser and creates a local dev token stored in ~/.redwood/token which the SDK will pick up. That avoids the cache-refresh path that trips org gating.

mika: Tried the CLI login — works! App starts and returns 200 on the Hello route. Thanks.

sam: Filed a follow-up to DEVEX-5189 to add clearer quickstart docs and a more helpful SDK error when refresh is blocked by billing (suggestion: surface "billing required" instead of opaque 403).

jordan: Also adding a short-term DX PR to the quickstart: detect 403 on refresh and print: "Your org needs billing/terms enabled — go to https://console.redwood.ai/orgs to resolve" with a link.

mika: That would have saved me 20 minutes. Will attach repro to the ticket.
